trails.trailTip: Arrive well before sunrise if you want a clear view — this short loop is the park's most popular sunrise photography spot and the small overlook fills up fast.
trails.didYouKnow: Mesa Arch frames a 500-foot drop and the La Sal Mountains beyond, making it one of the most photographed arches in Utah.

trails.trailTip: The trail hugs an unfenced rim in places, so keep kids and pets close, especially in wind.
trails.didYouKnow: Grand View Point looks out over the confluence country where the Green and Colorado Rivers carved Canyonlands' three districts apart.

trails.trailTip: No permit is needed for a day hike of this loop, but overnight camping at Chesler Park's designated sites requires a backcountry permit reserved in advance — as of September 2026, per NPS.gov — and there is no reliable water anywhere on the route, so carry at least 4 liters per person.
trails.didYouKnow: The Joint Trail section of this loop squeezes hikers through a sandstone fracture barely wider than a backpack for about 400 feet.

trails.trailTip: Bring sun protection — the trail to the second overlook has little shade and crosses open slickrock.
trails.didYouKnow: Geologists still debate whether Upheaval Dome is a collapsed salt dome or an ancient meteorite impact crater.

trails.trailTip: Carry a map or GPS track — this loop has long exposed stretches and cairned route-finding sections that are easy to lose in bright midday light.
trails.didYouKnow: The Syncline Loop circles Upheaval Dome entirely, dropping into and climbing back out of the crater basin.

trails.trailTip: This is a long day in exposed desert terrain with no reliable water source, so start early and carry more water than you think you'll need.
trails.didYouKnow: Druid Arch's massive, blocky form was named for its resemblance to the megaliths of Stonehenge.

trails.trailTip: This flat trail delivers a big payoff view without much elevation gain, but the overlook itself is unfenced, so keep an eye on kids near the edge.
trails.didYouKnow: The overlook takes its name from the pale White Rim sandstone bench visible far below, which also gives the famous White Rim jeep/bike road its name.

trails.estimatedTime: 5-6 hrs to White Rim Road and back
trails.trailTip: Lathrop drops nearly 1,600 feet from the Island in the Sky mesa to the White Rim bench, so budget extra time and water for the steep climb back out.
trails.didYouKnow: Lathrop Trail is one of only a few routes that connect the Island in the Sky mesa top down to the White Rim Road below.

animals.whereToLook: Canyon walls and mesas near the Colorado and Green River corridors
animals.viewingTip: During the fall rut, give rams extra space and watch any clashes from a distance with binoculars — approaching can provoke a defensive charge or spook the herd off precarious terrain.
animals.didYouKnow: Bighorn rams can weigh over 300 pounds, and their curled horns alone can weigh as much as all the bones in the rest of their body combined.

animals.whereToLook: Sunny slickrock outcrops throughout the park
animals.viewingTip: Watch from a few feet back with a zoom lens — collared lizards bask in the open but dart away instantly if crowded.
animals.didYouKnow: Collared lizards can run bipedally on their hind legs when startled, reaching impressive short bursts of speed.

animals.whereToLook: Thermals above mesa rims and canyon overlooks
animals.viewingTip: Scan the sky above rim overlooks with binoculars rather than approaching any cliff-edge nest site you might spot.
animals.didYouKnow: Golden eagles can spot a rabbit from over a mile away thanks to eyesight several times sharper than a human's.

animals.whereToLook: Desert flats and pinyon-juniper woodland, mostly after dark
animals.viewingTip: Kit foxes den underground and are rarely seen — if you spot tracks or a burrow, admire from a distance and never linger near or dig at a den entrance.
animals.didYouKnow: Kit foxes are the smallest fox species in North America, weighing as little as 3-6 pounds.

animals.viewingTip: Pronghorn are wary and fast — use binoculars from a pullout rather than approaching across open grassland.
animals.didYouKnow: Pronghorn evolved their speed to outrun now-extinct American cheetahs, far faster than any predator they face today.

animals.viewingTip: Watch from the trail with binoculars rather than following a deer off-trail for a closer photo.
animals.didYouKnow: Mule deer can jump all four legs simultaneously in a stiff-legged bound called 'stotting' while fleeing predators.

animals.whereToLook: Overlooks and picnic areas throughout the park
animals.viewingTip: Ravens are bold around people, but resist feeding them — human food makes them more aggressive around visitors and overlook parking areas.
animals.didYouKnow: Ravens are among the most intelligent birds, capable of problem-solving and tool use.

animals.whereToLook: Sunny slickrock ledges and rock crevices
animals.viewingTip: This venomous snake is small and well-camouflaged against pale slickrock — if you spot one, back away slowly and give it a wide berth rather than trying to move or handle it.
animals.didYouKnow: Despite its small size, the midget faded rattlesnake's venom is considered among the most potent of any North American rattlesnake.
